description:
Sieve is the routing table. No alias schema, no virtual domain map, no transport map. One language, one evaluator, one place to look when something routes wrong.

Key changes to current implementation:
1. Sieve evaluator runs per-recipient, not per-message. Current bug: sieve_delivery() uses only first recipient. Must be fixed — this is load-bearing for multi-domain routing.
2. Envelope variables pre-set before evaluation: ${envelope.from}, ${envelope.to}, ${envelope.to.localpart}, ${envelope.to.domain}
3. redirect action (RFC 5228 §4.2) — currently missing, must be added. Enqueues outbound SMTP delivery. Multiple redirect actions per script execution are valid. Does not consume message — fileinto and redirect can both fire.
4. Loop detection built into redirect from day one: X-Loop header check + hop counter in relay queue entry. Not retrofittable safely.
5. user_exists custom test: if user_exists :domain "kubernetes.io" { ... } — queries identities table for active identity with email at that domain.
6. System script stored in SQLite, one row, hot-reloaded on change. No restart required.
7. Per-user scripts: personal mailboxes only, evaluated after system script if system script does not stop.

Routing specificity (implicit, no integer priorities): exact address > local wildcard (security@*) > domain wildcard (*@kubernetes.io) > full wildcard (*@*). Within same tier: all matching rules fire in definition order, stopping at first reject.

SMTP session flow:
  RCPT TO → domain check → mailbox lookup → 550 if either fails
  DATA → buffer full body (accept-body-always decision, no pre-DATA Sieve pass)
  → evaluate system Sieve per recipient
  → evaluate per-user Sieve if personal mailbox
  → dispatch: fileinto → block store → JMAP index
              redirect → outbound SMTP queue
              reject → bounce
notes:
Personal mailbox redirect policy correction: user scripts CAN use redirect to external addresses by default. Blocking personal redirect is paternalistic and breaks legitimate use cases (forwarding work mail to personal inbox, etc).

The real concern is data exfiltration in high-security deployments, not personal redirect in general. Operator controls this, not the code.

Capability defaults:
  user = ["fileinto", "setflag", "vacation", "redirect"]  # redirect on by default

Operator restriction levers (all default permissive):
  [sieve.restrictions]
  user_redirect_internal_only = false   # if true, redirect only to domains in domains table
  user_redirect_domains = []            # empty = any domain allowed; set to whitelist specific domains
  user_redirect_min_trust_block = "hardware"  # mailboxes at this trust level or above block redirect regardless of user script or global settings

Three independent levers, all default permissive. Classified mailbox (min_trust_level=hardware) blocks redirect unconditionally — contents of a hardware-tier mailbox should not forward to gmail.com regardless of user preference or global operator setting. Operator tightens for high-security deployments. Generic community operator leaves defaults alone.
title: design: Sieve-primary routing — system script, per-recipient evaluation, redirect action
